DATA_REQUIRED (non-blocking): the mapping RC2 endpoint -> ArduPlane pitch-up vs pitch-down demand is not separately documented in this repository. This test therefore classifies scenarios C/D by the measured sign of nav_pitch_deg (the demand ArduPlane actually formed), not by the RC endpoint. The elevator sign chain is validated against the demand, so the conclusion does not depend on resolving this.

E.name: yaw_right

pre_registered_expectation.expected_yaw_rate_sign: - in FLU body frame (nose right is a NEGATIVE rotation about +Z-up); + in the MAVLink FRD yawspeed field
pre_registered_expectation.source: SITL_TRANSPORT_AND_ACTUATOR_MAPPING.md sec 7.3 + CONTROLS.md sec 10 + 2026-08-22 report tests 7/9

checks.note: positive rudder joint = TE toward -Y = RIGHT
Cn<0 <=> Mz<0 <=> nose right (FLU)
MAVLink FRD: nose-right is POSITIVE yaw rate

FLU body frame: nose-right is a NEGATIVE rotation about +Z-up. This is the SAME physical motion as the MAVLink check above, expressed in the other convention - the opposite expected sign here is the frame conversion, not a contradiction.

KFF_RDDRMIX is a roll->rudder feedforward, NOT rudder->roll, so a rudder input should not directly drive the ailerons; any aileron motion here is FBWA holding wings level against the yaw-roll coupling, which is expected and is reported rather than judged.
